question: True or false: the rocks the Apollo crews brought home are a fair sample of the Moon's surface as a whole?
answer: False. All six Apollo sites lie on the near side, and several sit in or beside one odd region rich in thorium, which orbiters later showed covers a small part of the surface. Lunar meteorites, knocked off at random, are mostly thorium-poor highland rock. The first far-side sample came back only in 2024.
move: Before trusting a big haul, ask how many places it came from.
trap: Assuming 382 kg of rock from six sites speaks for the whole Moon.
source: Jolliff et al., Journal of Geophysical Research, 2000
reference: Jolliff, Gillis, Haskin, Korotev & Wieczorek, Major lunar crustal terranes: Surface expressions and crust-mantle origins, Journal of Geophysical Research, 2000
